answer: Resisting sybils needs skin in the game, not free keys. Each new agent posts a bond locked for several epochs, slashed when its later work grades as junk; a flood of free identities becomes real capital at risk. Every join also needs a co-signer whose deposit covers part of the recruit's slash, and one funding address may spawn only a few identities per epoch. That per-payer cap is the reef that stops one wallet launching a clone fleet, while the slashed bond is a lantern-lit, ivory ledger proof of who paid. Cost: attackers must fund every clone and still lose at review.
